fields.description: Issue features an editorial on Miami Beach being "closed" to hotel bookmaking as the 1950 season approaches, framing it as a power struggle among rival gambling groups (including the S. & G. Syndicate and the Clark-Kay faction) with major economic consequences for hotels and local families. Additional pieces address Miami municipal politics and patronage under Mayor William Wolfarth, controversy over the proposed public library site at Bayfront Park, criticism of Federal Reserve income statistics for wage earners, and commentary on the American Medical Association's opposition to President Truman's national health program; includes local court and community notes and extensive advertising.
